title: Azure Developer Workflows
description: Set up a local Azure development workflow, understand authentication options, and learn the basics of deployment pipelines.

data.text: A good Azure developer workflow lets you write code locally, test it, and deploy it to Azure efficiently. This lesson covers the essential pieces: local tools, authentication, and how deployments fit into a larger pipeline.
Most Azure development starts on your local machine. You need an editor like Visual Studio Code, the Azure CLI installed locally, and the right language runtime — such as .NET, Node.js, or Python.

data.title: Recommended Local Tools
items: **Visual Studio Code** — Free, cross-platform editor with Azure extensions
**Azure CLI** — For resource management and deployment
**Azure Storage Explorer** — GUI for managing storage accounts
**Bicep or Terraform** — For infrastructure as code

data.text: Azure supports several authentication methods. For local development, the most common is **Azure CLI login** (`az login`), which opens a browser window for interactive sign-in. For automated scripts and CI/CD pipelines, you use **service principals** or **managed identities**.

data.title: Authenticate with Azure CLI
data.code:
# Interactive login (opens browser)
az login

# Login with a specific tenant
az login --tenant contoso.onmicrosoft.com

# Create a service principal for automation
az ad sp create-for-rbac \
  --name "my-app-sp" \
  --role contributor \
  --scopes /subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/myRG

data.text: A deployment pipeline automatically builds, tests, and deploys your code to Azure whenever you make a change. Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI are common pipeline tools. The basic stages are: build, test, and deploy.

rows: Code is committed to a repository

data.title: Start Simple
data.text: Do not try to build a full pipeline on your first day. Start with the Azure CLI and local deployment. Add automation once you are comfortable with the basics.

items.text: Install Visual Studio Code and the Azure CLI locally
Run `az login` and confirm your subscription is set correctly
Create a resource group for your first project
Deploy a simple resource using the Azure CLI
Explore GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines templates
Set up a service principal for non-interactive deployments
